rationale: Round 1 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so round 2 raises aggressiveness across all seven passes while keeping cost weights below the security weights so hot-path damage stays bounded. FLA and ICALL get the highest SecurityGain because methcall's structure is tiny dispatch-driven virtual calls (Toggle/nth_toggle_activate) inside a hot loop — flattening the few small bodies and indirecting the call targets directly attacks the program's reverse-engineering crux; ICALL's RuntimeCost is capped at 0.5 so the per-iteration dispatch overhead stays acceptable, and its CorrectnessRisk is the highest of the table (0.4) to keep the selector cautious around the struct-pointer call sites. BCF keeps a solid SecurityGain with moderately elevated Runtime/SizeCost weights since bogus predicates on 30-256 byte functions inflate size quickly, and IGV stays the weakest pass because this benchmark has almost no global state to protect. SUB and SPLIT remain near-free diversity sources and are pushed hardest on DiversityGain, letting the selector layer cheap obfuscation everywhere while the expensive passes concentrate on the call-dispatch and control-flow hotspots.
